subject: Statistical power / how many loci given X samples?

messages.author: 6a8f96be35217d76
messages.subject: Statistical power / how many loci given X samples?
parts:
Hi all,

A colleague of mine mentioned in passing, they used poppr to estimate how many loci to use given X samples, i.e., the statistical power of the experiment. They did not confine how that was accrued. I failed to find this information in the latest manual / online Intro. Any pointers are highly appreciated, as I'm setting up a chain of major studies (up to 1,200 Inds).

Thanks in advance!
-M

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Statistical power / how many loci given X samples?
parts:
Hello M,

What your colleague might be referring to is the genotype accumulation curve: https://grunwaldlab.github.io/poppr/reference/genotype_curve.html

This curve is primarily useful for clonal data sets and can tell you if you have selected enough loci to resolve all of the unique multilocus genotypes in your sample. Arnaud-Haond et al 2007 describe its use well, IMO
https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1365-294X.2007.03535.x

HI M,

while not related to poppr (hope it's ok to post :) ), you might be interested in this power analysis software:
http://www.congressgenetics.eu/page.aspx?SP=Simulator_Start
It is designed for optimization of sampling strategy for five common genetic study topics: hybridization, temporal sampling, bottlenecks, connectivity and assignment.

Here's also the accompanying paper:
https://besjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/2041-210x.12025
